articleTitle: Sizing a Heterogeneous Battery System for an Offshore Vessel: Methodology and Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Waterborne transport sector is essential to our everyday life as ships deliver more than 80% of the world's trade. Electrification of waterborne transport with batteries is the focus of the current paper. Battery systems for vessels tend to be monotype and hence are oversized to meet the vessel operational profile and lifetime requirements. Heterogeneous battery systems offer a solution to that challenge by better fitting the vessel requirements. The present paper details a methodology to size a heterogeneous battery energy storage system made of high-energy (HE) and high-power (HP) battery modules. The methodology is then applied to a real case study of an offshore vessel to be hybridised with a 1MWh battery solution. The resulting HE and HP share is 18% / 82% respectively.

articleTitle: Maximizing the Energy-Saving Potential of Declutchable Bev Powertrains Via Eco-Driving
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Compared to a conventional BEV powertrain, a declutchable powertrain integrating a clutch mechanism can mechanically disconnect the electric drive unit (EDU) from the drive axle. By disengaging the clutch, the vehicle can realize the free-coasting feature, which utilizes vehicle kinetic energy while mitigating the no-load losses of the EDU. In order to maximize the energy-saving potential of such feature, this paper proposes an Eco-driving strategy based on model predictive control (MPC) specifically tailored for the declutchable BEV powertrain. The effectiveness of the proposed strategy is assessed through simulation studies over three representative real-world routes. Finally, the energy consumption of the declutchable powertrain is then compared to that of a conventional BEV powertrain employing a standard Eco-driving strategy, showcasing the value of the declutchable BEV powertrain.

articleTitle: Electric Road Systems for Electric Vehicle Long-Distance Travel: A Multi-Agent Simulation Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Electric road systems (ERSs) present a transformative advancement in transportation electrification, offering continuous charging capabilities for electric vehicles (EVs) during travel. This innovation has the potential to significantly mitigate range anxiety by enabling in-motion charging, thereby enhancing the overall efficiency of electric mobility, and reducing the frequency of charging stops during long-distance trips. By decreasing the need for larger EV batteries, ERS can also contribute to lower emissions. This paper details the implementation of ERS within the multi-agent transportation simulation (MATSim) framework, leveraging the EV-Contrib library to assess ERS as a viable charging infrastructure for long-distance EV travels. The results provide an evaluation of ERS deployment and its impact on dynamic charging behaviors.

articleTitle: Kinetic Energy Recovery System for Electric Buses: A Method for Extending Mileage Range
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel system for electric buses (EBs) that utilizes an Airflow Kinetic Energy Recovery System (Air-KERS) to capture kinetic energy from the forward motion of the bus. The Air-KERS consists of a generator array with blades that rotate due to the airflow, generating electricity to recharge the battery. The analysis, calculations, and simulations presented support the feasibility of this concept. However, a key challenge is maintaining the required airflow speed for the generator array to operate optimally. The study proposes integrating air ducts, with the optimal placement found to be at the bottom of the EB due to the minimal drag coefficient. The research investigates the system's performance across three driving cycles, demonstrating a potential range increase of 2% with an efficiency range of 70–90% depending on the bus speed.

articleTitle: Reverse Engineering-Based Modeling of an EV Motor Drive for Digital Twin Development
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Digital twins (DTs) play crucial roles in various applications, with their significance extending to critical domains like electric vehicles (EVs). Essentially, a DT is a virtual representation or digital counterpart of a physical object, system, or process, crafted through sensor technology, data collection, modeling, and simulation. Modeling a real system with uncertain parameters is a challenging task. This paper presents a comprehensive methodology for reverse engineering the drive system of an EV Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) with an uncertain control strategy parameter. The motor was modeled based on d-q mathematical representation. Extensive tests on the EV motor drive under diverse conditions and scenarios were conducted, with performance data acquired using a precision data acquisition system (DAS). The collected data were preprocessed and refined for the modeling process. In response to feedback on input mechanisms, a data-driven model employing a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network was developed to emulate the drive system's behavior. The LSTM-based drive system model underwent rigorous training with the actual data collected from the physical system. The overall accuracy of the LSTM model in replicating the motor drive system was 96.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, affirming its high performance and reliability in mimicking the intricate drive system. The LSTM model was then combined with the motor simulation model, creating a hybrid-driven model. The hybrid model's success in closely aligning with the actual motor drive outputs underscores its comprehensive ability to effectively reflect both the nuanced dynamics and the operational intricacies of the EV propulsion system.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Passive and Active Equalizers for Lithium-Ion Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: In recent years, approximately hundred topologies have been studied for Li-ion cell balance. In this paper, some equalizer topologies, comprising classical passive and active equalizers, are considered. The comparison considered several aspects, and for each of them, different Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) were defined. The most important KPIs are related to balancing time, capacity reduction due to balancing, weight, cost and volume. Finally, the KPIs were compared to select the topology with the best performance.

articleTitle: Train Control System Independent of Communication Transmission Paths
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: With recent labor shortages in the railway industry, there is a growing need for the streamlining of equipment maintenance in Japan. Currently, many train control systems rely on proprietary networks that use rail current in track circuits for transmission, resulting in costly operation and maintenance of onboard equipment and ground equipment. In order to realize a low-cost train control system, this paper proposed the separation of the security control function and the information transmission function by using public communication lines, which are the most versatile information transmission lines, by offering the prospect of reducing the number of self-owned equipment, including cables, radios, and antennas, in addition, proposed the design policy of a train control system that can adjust the stability of communication transmission paths as the situation demands.

articleTitle: Vehicle to Grid from the Electric Vehicle Point-of-View to Reduce Peak Demand and System Cost
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The study presents Electric Vehicle (EV) Point-of-View (POV) Vehicle to Grid (V2G) optimisation, where the system knows the trips and energy demand of the EV. This allows it to be less conservative in the departure State of Charge (SoC) of the EV battery. The peak and cost reduction of Vehicle POV optimisation are compared with state-of-the-art Location Point-of-View optimisation, this is, the car can do V2G but it has to depart each location with at least 80% SoC as the next trip energy demand is unknown. A Mix Integer Linear Programming (MILP) V2G optimisation approach is presented to reduce peak demand and total system cost of a fleet of EVs travelling between several residential locations and one common workplace. Simulations were conducted with 26 EVs unevenly distributed between five residential locations and commuters to a common workplace. The results indicate little differences in the reduction of peak demand between both POVs of V2G optimisation. However, the system cost can be further reduced with Vehicle Point-of-View optimization, saving an additional 200 euros annually per household by transporting cheaper energy from workplaces to residential locations.

articleTitle: A Multi-Objective Co-Design Optimization Framework for Microgrid Architecture in Marine Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Multi-objective optimization of the battery energy storage system (BESS) microgrid architecture in the marine sector is crucial, considering the immense power demand and multiple possible electrical/electronic topologies. As a result, various steps are often taken to simplify the design problem, limit the size of the design space, and make separate optimizations in different components and converters. However, the first step is to properly size and design the microgrid architecture. This paper proposes a multi-objective co-design optimization framework for the optimal selection of the microgrid and power electronic (PE) architecture in a vessel's BESS. For this purpose, a non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-II) optimization, in addition to the Pareto Search, is used to generate all the possible solutions and then illustrate the optimal points, which enables a trade-off between the total initial cost of PEs and total converter losses as objectives. The cost function that leads to the optimum architecture selection considers capital cost and efficiency objectives. The interoperable framework is applied considering four different DC/AC architectures. Finally, from the objective perspective, the globally best architecture is determined as the framework's output.

articleTitle: Design and Method for an Experimental Setup to Evaluate the Heat Transfer in a Watercooled Eddy Current Brake
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: In this article the design and the method for an experimental setup to investigate the heat transfer of eddy current brakes with anisotropic structure is presented. In order to determine the heat transfer coefficient, the wall temperature is calculated using the temperature-dependent electrical resistance. The heat is induced by Joule heating. A coupled 3D multiphysics single flow simulation setup is used to investigate the temperature profile along the length. With this method it is possible to design and set up an experiment to investigate the flow boiling heat transfer coefficient in a eddy current brake with anisotropic material structure.

articleTitle: A Mixed-Integer Charging Schedule for Electric Vehicles with Request-Dependent Pricing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: A pricing mechanism for the charging schedule problem of Electric Vehicles (EVs) that takes into account the requests of EVs is proposed. Conventional price schemes adopted in the literature are typically affected by total energy demand and the time of use (TOU) tariff. These models do not capture the fact that, in real-world booking systems, by increasing the request in the presence of fixed limited resources, the price increases. In this paper, we propose a price function that, in addition to considering the effect of total energy demand and TOU tariff, it also accounts for satisfied and dissatisfied EVs due to fixed finite resources. The problem is modeled by using a mixed-integer linear cooperative structure by including the presence of infrastructural limitations such as the number of chargers and maximum demand from the grid. A corresponding optimization problem is defined whose cost function aims to reach a compromise between the demand from the grid during peak hours and the level of dissatisfaction with electric vehicles. Simulation results show that the proposed pricing mechanism, which also accounts for resource limitation, does not have adverse effects on energy peak shaving and allows a realistic balance for EV charging satisfaction.

articleTitle: Parameter Determination of Synchronous Generators using Load Angle Estimation Considering Saturation Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Parameter determination of synchronous generators is necessary for power system analysis and also for control system regulation. Load angle estimation of synchronous generators needs a rotor position sensor that is challenging to implement is real power plants. In first step, this paper introduces an indirect integral calculation method to estimate the load angle without any rotor position sensor. In second step, this paper introduces a procedure to determine steady state reactance of synchronous generator considering the core saturation effect using known load angle value from first step. The main advantage of this method is that it is sensor-less and does not need the generator to disconnect from network and the test is done when the generator is synchronized. In addition, the proposed method estimates the unsaturated and saturated values of reactance on both d and q axis. The proposed method is evaluated by FE simulation of a 255MW synchronous generator.

articleTitle: Multilevel Inverter for EV Charging via Hybrid Storage Unit (Fuel Cell, Battery, Ultracapacitor)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper deals with the design and numerical simulation of a multilevel inverter used for EV charging. A mobile charging station (MCS) is our application. The MCS is to be analyzed while being equipped with a fuel cell, and/or battery, and/or a supercapacitor, used to transfer the electric energy towards a battery type EV. A high-power multilevel inverter topology is proposed, to assure up to 43 kW ac charging (also called the 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> ac charging mode), while complying with the IEC 61000-2-2 standard in terms of harmonic and amplitude for the 3-phase currents and voltages. For ordinary two-level inverters, a high power (with important costs and volume) LCL filter is needed. The motivation of using the multilevel converter (a 3-level one) resides on the necessity of assuring the charging energy quality standard with reduced volume, mass and cost for the filter, while accepting a more complex converter structure (with double number of switches). The study will be focused on the topologies of multilevel inverters (especially on the 3-level inverter), on the design of its filter and on the simulated results, while considering different storage units (fuel cell, battery and supercapacitor), in the 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> ac charging mode of EVs.

articleTitle: Inner Claw-Pole Stator Outer PM Rotor Small Synchronous Motor/Actuator for Vehicular Service Technologies: 3D-FEM Simulation and Experimental Tests
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: As vehicular modern electric technologies imply the need for ever better auxiliary services, small electric actuators with higher energy conversion performance at affordable prices are required. This paper introduces a three-phase inner claw pole ATOMET core stator with outer PM rotor synchronous actuator characterized by a modular structure with one circular shape AC coil per phase, capable to produce high torque per copper loss and enjoy a practical fabrication at reasonable cost. The core of the paper includes the key 3D-FEM validation with preliminary experimental results on a dedicated laboratory prototype at 125W, 700rpm.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Inductive Charging Systems for Electric Buses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: A comparative analysis of multi- coil transmitter inductive power system for electric buses is proposed in the paper. The goal of the analysis is to identify the behavior of aircore multi-coils transmitter in alignment and misalignment conditions that are often present in the considered application, comparing the results with the standard case of single coil transmitter. The analysis is carried out using analytical models for the wireless power system and finite element analysis to calculate the main electrical parameters necessary to identify the model. A case study is analyzed referring to a transmitter and a receiver with a square coil in order to evaluate the qualitative behavior of the system.

articleTitle: Loss Characteristics of PMSM Drive System for Inverter Switching
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The demand for energy conservation has led to a need for higher efficiency in the permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drive system, including the inverter. To date, studies have focused on the trade-off between inverter switching losses and motor copper and iron losses. Focusing on the recent development of power semiconductor devices, higher breakdown voltages, and lower losses have been realized. Therefore, in this trade-off relationship in the future, increasing the switching frequency and reducing motor losses are expected to lead to higher efficiency of the PMSM drive system. In this study, PMSM drive system losses were measured and analyzed in a system of a 1 kW PMSM and insulated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) inverter when driven in the asynchronous pulse width modulation (PWM) carrier frequency of 10 kHz and the synchronous PWM 3-pulse mode. The results reveal that effectively reducing motor losses by increasing the switching frequency is more effective for the efficiency of the PMSM drive system than reducing inverter losses by decreasing the switching frequency.

articleTitle: Development of 1 MW Hybrid Electric Propulsion Drive System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Aircraft electric propulsion electrical machine drives have recently been studied and developed by academics and industry. As the weight penalty is much higher in aerospace applications compared to the automotive counterpart, optimizing power density is a critical part of electrical drive system design. A Permanent Magnet (PM) drive system rated for 1 MW has been developed for flight demonstrations of two different electric hybrid propulsion systems, Hybrid Electric Propulsion (HEP) and Electrically Assisted Propulsion (EAP), where challenges exist in close integration with aircraft engines. In the HEP system, the electrical machine is integrated with an internal combustion engine via a gearbox in a parallel hybrid configuration. In the EAP system, two electrical machines are integrated with a turbofan jet engine, one machine being installed on the high pressure spool and the other on the low pressure spool, enabling power transfer between the spools by electrical means. The electrical machine is driven and controlled by a T-Type three-level inverter which has 2 x 3-phase outputs with a minimized DC-link filter using phase shifted PWM switching. The machine is an oil cooled surface PM type with distributed windings with a fundamental frequency of 1.2 kHz. Litz conductors wrapped with Kapton tape are used to minimize AC losses and increase the partial discharge inception voltage. Both the controller and machine are designed for partial discharge free operation in all flight conditions validated by electric field analysis. This paper discusses the details of the drive system and presents test results from a dynamometer, which has demonstrated a machine peak power density of 10 kW/kg and drive system efficiency exceeding 95%.

articleTitle: Optimization of Sensor Setup and Filter Frequency for End-of-Line Partial Discharge Testing of Electrical Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Repetitive partial discharges (PDs) occurring within minor faults in the insulation system of an electrical machine accelerate insulation degeneration and cause premature failure. Therefore, reliable PD testing is crucial at the end of the production line for automotive traction machines to ensure the required service life. However, the PD detection capability and the test results depend on the sensitivity of the utilized sensors. This paper thoroughly assesses various sensor setups, including ultrahigh frequency (UHF) antennas and a high-frequency current transformer (HFCT), to identify the optimal test configuration for automotive hairpin stators. First, an optimization procedure is introduced to determine the most appropriate frequency range for each sensor to detect PD. In addition, an analysis of noise interference is conducted. Secondly, the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and the repetitive partial discharge inception voltage (RPDIV), as defined in IEC/TS 61934, are compared for the HFCT and different antennas at varying positions and distances. The HFCT has been found to have the highest sensitivity, resulting in lower RPDIV values in most test runs. Broadband UHF antennas provide a higher SNR than the antenna of the commercial PD tester, which only utilizes a narrow frequency band for PD detection. The sensitivity of all antennas under consideration increases when the distance to the test object is reduced. Synchronous acquisition with two identical antennas at different positions or a combined evaluation of the HFCT and an antenna promises a more reliable PD detection for a few test objects. Further, the choice of the sensor cannot systematically influence the RPDIV variation of several consecutive test runs, as the stochastic nature of PD occurrence causes this variation.

articleTitle: Extraction of Ferrite Material Properties and Application to Simulation-Based Common-Mode Filter Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The insertion impedance of common-mode chokes (CMC) is defined by the core material's permeability, permittivity and geometrical shape. The datasheet information on material properties is often insufficient, as it is function to manufacturing process, wide tolerances and defined only in a certain frequency range. A core's geometry can be optimized for a specific application by simulation, but only if the material is well known. This work demonstrates how to extract complex permeability and permittivity data by measurement, employing an impedance analyzer with commercial magnetic material test fixture or with self-built fixture and analytic formulas in order to predict the common-mode impedance for a custom core shape. Further, we present a measurement setup employing an vector network analyzer to obtain modal (common-mode and differential-mode) impedances of chokes with different core shapes and derive an equivalent circuit for transient or frequency-domain simulation. The extracted material data is also used to create a 3D electromagnetic simulation model. The different modelling and simulation approaches are compared by application to a 300 A CMC for power electronics.

articleTitle: Short-Circuit DC Current Estimation of Hybrid Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: DC microgrids have become a valuable alternative to AC microgrids for industrial and shipboard power systems due to the DC nature of most energy storage systems, which are increasingly used in these applications. However, integrating this technology introduces new protection issues. The unidirectionality and the very high derivative of DC fault currents discharging from the capacitor are the main challenges arising from adopting DC technology. Therefore, this study focuses on the short-circuit response of energy storage systems and their power electronic converters. Several energy storage sources are modeled using manufacturers datasheets, and their short-circuit responses are analyzed. The short-circuit responses of each energy storage system are simulated and compared with an analytical method. A parametric study is then performed, varying selected parameters to examine their influence on the short-circuit response.

articleTitle: Power Converter Modulation for Battery Soc Estimation in Electric Vehicle Powertrains: a Torque Ripple Minimization Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The Battery Management System (BMS) in electric vehicles (EVs) is essential for accurate battery state of charge (SoC) estimation. Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EiS) is a proven method for this, but its traditional use has been limited to laboratories due to expensive, bulky equipment. Recent advancements, however, have made it possible to adapt EIS for on-board EV applications. This study presents a novel SoC estimation technique for lithium-ion batteries, designed for integration into EV powertrains, particularly those using Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSM). By leveraging field-oriented control (FOC), the method injects an alternating current (AC) perturbation into the direct-axis (d-axis) stator current to generate the EIS signal. The accuracy of this technique is validated against traditional laboratory-based EIS methods. A challenge of this approach is the torque ripple it produces, which can impact vehicle performance. To address this, the paper introduces a torque ripple minimization strategy using a proportional-resonant (PR) controller. This method is particularly relevant as companies like Tesla, BMW, and Nissan increasingly use PMSM in their EVs, highlighting the broader applicability of this technique.

articleTitle: The Static Phase Converter. A Solution to Reinforce the Power Supply of 25 kV/ 50Hz Railway Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Despite its benefits compared to its competitors, the 25 kV - 50 Hz railway electrification system suffers some drawbacks. In particular, it produces a voltage unbalance on the three-phase power grid, and adjacent substations cannot operate in parallel which prohibits power sharing. In critical cases, the implementation of a power electronic substation, hereinafter referred as Static Phase Converter (SPC), can be a solution. This paper focuses on the integration of a SPC on a sector of 25 kV railway line. Simulations are performed on a generic case.

articleTitle: An Improved Feature-Position-Based Sensorless Direct Torque Control Scheme for SRM Drives at Medium-High Speeds
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel sensorless direct torque control (DTC) method based on the inductance inflection point to improve the torque performance and enhance the reliability of the switched reluctance motor. The conventional sensorless methods suffer the required prior knowledge, modelling complexity, and computational burden. A straightforward sensorless approach utilizing feature position is developed to identify the phase commutation point and implement DTC for torque ripple mitigation. Furthermore, the impact of the saturation effect is considered for accurate position detection and torque estimation. The proposed sensorless DTC method is verified by simulation in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Adaptive Controller Design and Power Loss Analysis of Resistive and Inductive Cell Balancing During Static, Charging, and Discharging Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: A key feature of a battery management system is cell balancing for series-connected lithium-ion cells. Numerous cell balancing methods have been studied in the literature and are categorised into two categories: active and passive. The cheapest and simplest method of cell balancing without complex management is passive cell balancing, although it wastes energy through heat generation and leaves room for overcharge and discharge owing to a lack of control. There are many active cell balancing topologies available, but the one that is being presented is based on a single inductor, which has the advantages of requiring the fewest possible components, being inexpensive, being tiny, and having high efficiency and quick cell balancing speed. The fundamental resistor cell balancing technique is also implemented. The battery pack is made up of four series-connected cells. To test the accuracy of the balancing topology, each cell has a unique initial SOC condition. Two cases and three operating modes-static, charging, and discharging-have been tested. The balance time and switching frequency are both fixed, and power loss calculations are performed to compare the effectiveness of the two approaches.

articleTitle: Regenerative Braking Capabilities in E-Bike Vehicles: Comparison Between two Drive Architectures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: A comparative study between two regenerative braking strategies implemented on a 100 kg (bike + user) overall mass e-bike system is presented. The simulation models are built in MATLAB Simulink® environment and a commercial in-wheel direct-drive brushless DC (BLDC) motor is assumed as benchmark electrical machine. In the paper, a brief literature review about regenerative braking is firstly presented. Secondly a simulation comparison between two drive schemes is reported. The first scheme is composed by a buck converter and an inverter with six-step commutation. The second scheme, however, doesn't have the buck converter and uses two different Pulse Width Modulation techniques to control the inverter for motoring function and electric braking function. The aim of the work is to study the possibilities of the implementation and the advantages of this kind of brake, useful for extending the autonomy range of a LEV.

articleTitle: Position Estimation for Sinusoidal Doubly Salient Electromagnetic Machine Considering Crosscoupling Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Aiming at the defects of traditional highfrequency (HF) voltage injection method, such as relying on the saliency of rotor, complex demodulation processes, and estimation accuracy susceptible to cross-coupling effect, a method for estimating the rotor position of sinusoidal doubly salient electromagnetic machine (SDSEM) by injecting HF voltage into its excitation windings with angle compensation for cross-coupling effect is proposed. Firstly, a mathematical model of SDSEM considering cross-coupling effect is established. Then, based on the mutual inductance characteristic between excitation windings and armature windings of SDSEM, the HF voltage signal is injected into excitation windings and the rotor position is estimated by the HF resulting current of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>-axis and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-axis. Next, the influence of cross-coupling effect on the accuracy of the proposed position estimation method with HF voltage injection is analyzed. The cross-coupling angle caused by this effect is calculated by using online method, and the angle compensation is carried out during sensorless control. Finally, simulation results show that the proposed method effectively reduces the DC bias error of position estimation under various speeds and load conditions, enhancing position estimation accuracy and demonstrating good steady-state and dynamic following performance.

articleTitle: Simplified Thermal Identification and Modelling of Li-PO Batteries for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Fixed wing UAVs (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) with VTOL (Vertical Take Off and Landing) are often equipped with hybrid propulsion and energy management systems in which lithium cells are subjected to quite discontinuous loading profile (short peaks with prolonged periods of relatively negligible loads). Electric performances of these storage systems can be strongly affected by their thermal behavior. In this work authors introduce the preliminary study of simplified identification and modelling procedures that should be applied on commercial lithium polymer cells in a way that is compatible with the fast development of innovative prototypes.

Author Keywords: Thermal Modelling and Identification of Batteries

articleTitle: Battery Modeling for Road Vehicles Application: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of three different lithium-ion battery modeling approaches for electric vehicle applications. The Shepherd analytical model is compared with the zero-order and first-order equivalent circuit models to identify an approach that offers a tradeoff between accuracy and complexity. The study concludes that models that do not require experimental testing for parameterization can be used for the initial sizing of a battery pack, while models based on experimental identification are more accurate and can be used, together with the former, if the sizing process needs to take into account the dynamics of the system. Overall, the paper highlights the importance of considering both accuracy and complexity when selecting a lithium-ion battery modeling approach for electric vehicle applications.

articleTitle: Impacts of using Different Semiconductor Technologies on Drivetrain Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: In electric passenger vehicles with modest performance the drivetrain usually consists of one inverter, one electrical machine and a single-speed transmission. The inverter is typically a two-level inverter using either Si IGBT transistors with an anti-parallel Si diode, or a SiC MOSFET transistor with or without an anti-parallel diode. The benefits of selecting SiC MOSFET as semiconductor technology are clear: increased efficiency and better thermal properties. The benefit of Si IGBT is lower cost for the manufacturer. However, a fair comparison must consider drivetrains that have been optimised with the different semiconductors in mind since it is the system level cost and efficiency that is most interesting from a vehicle-level perspective. In this paper, the production and running cost of drivetrains using Si IGBT and SiC MOSFET are compared. Furthermore, the paper includes a cost model for traction inverters that has been developed in collaboration with a large industrial partner in the automotive industry.

articleTitle: Hybrid Ship Fuel Consumption Prediction Through Operational Performance Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The maritime industry's imperative to optimize fuel consumption and reduce environmental impact necessitates the development of advanced predictive models for ship operational performance. This paper presents an approach to address this challenge through the integration of hybrid modeling techniques and Siemens Simcenter Amesim software. The primary objective is to develop a hybrid ship functional model capable of accurately predicting fuel consumption across diverse seaway scenarios.

articleTitle: System Model for Initial Charging of a New Battery Set Using Grid and Solar Pv System for Railway Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper is focused on solving the existing practices for charging a new Lead-acid battery set before actually using it for signalling related operations and power circuits of diesel locomotives in Railways. The primary objective is to use renewable energy sources during the charging cycle and also utilize the energy waste during the discharging cycle. Instead of wasting that energy, we can transfer it to the grid to generate revenue from it or utilize it to meet the demand of DC load of a railway station. For the charge cycle, a PV panel is used during the day and a single-phase grid is used during the night to charge the battery set in this proposed Simulink model. For the discharge cycle, grid and DC loads are used to discharge the battery set. To replace the existing manual process, a state flow control logic is designed to work according to the standard process of initial charging a battery set. It is observed that the proposed method can save around 4910.902 MWh of energy compared to the existing practice taking place in Indian Railways.

articleTitle: A Diagnosis Method for Open-Switch Faults in Open-Winding Sinusoidal Doubly Salient Electromagnetic Machine Drive System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Sinusoidal Doubly Salient Electromagnetic Machine (SDSEM) has simple structure, high reliability, high temperature and high speed operation ability. It has good application prospects in aerospace, rail transit, electric vehicles and other fields. Compared with the single inverter drive system, the open-winding SDSEM drive system has better operation performance and stronger fault-tolerant operation ability. However, the redundant operation characteristics of the open-winding topology make the fault diagnosis of the switch more difficult. To address the issues of slow diagnosis speed, high diagnosis cost, and complex fault localization in existing diagnosis methods for open-switch faults in the common-bus open-winding motor drive system, this paper proposes a diagnosis method based on diagnostic pulse self-injection. Firstly, the mathematical model of SDSEM and the common-bus open-winding motor drive system are introduced. Secondly, the phase current characteristics of the open-winding SDSEM drive system after the open-switch faults are analyzed. Then, according to the current characteristics of SDSEM in normal operation and fault state, the fault detection is carried out, and the response current is generated on the phase winding by the back electromotive force (EMF) of the motor to realize the self-injection of the diagnostic pulse, so as to locate the fault switch. Finally, the correctness and feasibility of the proposed method are verified by simulations.

Author Keywords: per-unit average value of phase current

articleTitle: Electric Power Prediction of 2D FE Magnetic Spring Energy Harvester Based on Coil using Support Vector Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Magnetic spring energy harvesters are considered to be a promising solution for powering small electronic devices because they employ the magnetic interaction between two fixed permanent magnets and one that is levitated vertically. This paper presents the two dimensional (2D) Finite Element Method (FEM) model of magnetic spring energy harvester based on coil layout. The simulation provides an optimized arrangement of number of turn and geometrical parameters of coil in the magnetic spring. The method based on Support Vector Machine (SVM) is proposed to predict electrical power of magnetic spring and to establish its dependence on the coil parameters. Furthermore an experimental analysis was performed to evaluate the electrical performance of the proposed magnetic spring system.

articleTitle: A Method for Determining Substation Output Voltage for Energy Saving Focused on Regenerative Train FC Voltage in DC-Electrified Railway
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: In DC-electrified railway, when the substation output voltage is high, the train voltage increases, and light-load regenerative brake control is activated, resulting in a decrease in the regenerative energy. When the substation output voltage is low, the main circuit loss and power loss increase owing to the increase in the acceleration time and current. Therefore, the substation output voltage that maximizes the energy-saving effect is determined by the trade-off relationship between regenerative energy and consumed energy. The purpose of this study is to focus on the correlation between the regenerative vehicle FC voltage and regenerative energy reduction and its position dependence, and to propose a method for determining the output voltage of multiple substations that can maximize the regenerative power beyond substations. The proposed method reduces the number of voltage parameters, which contributes to a considerable reduction in the number of simulations.

articleTitle: Air Gap Field Comparison of Hybrid and Electrical Excited Synchronous Machines Without Rare Earth Magnets for Use in Road Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The individual mobility is changing from fuel to battery electric drive. During the run-up of the technology the pollution and the accessibility of resources get into focus. The object of this paper is a comparison of two hybrid excited synchronous machines (HESM). To support the environmental goals rare earth free ferrite magnets are used. In a first step an analytical basic simulation of the air gap field was done. There an approximation of potential of the HESM with magnets in tooth and HESM tangential/radial flux (HESM TR) was cal-culated. Second step is the measurement of the magnetic field in a test pattern. A changeable rotor enables the measurement of the HESM and an electrical excited synchronous machine (EESM) in one stator.

articleTitle: Quasi-Square-Wave PWM Modulation for Modular Multilevel Converter in Variable Speed Motor Drives With Self Voltage Recovery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This article presents a detailed analysis of the Quasi-Square-Wave (QSW) PWM-modulated Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) inverter used in variable-speed motor drive systems. Through an examination of inserted arm behavior, this study investigates the effects of sub-module capacitance, arm inductance, and delay time on capacitor voltage overshoot. It introduces a component design technique that significantly reduces the requirements for capacitance and inductance, surpassing the capabilities of existing QSW-PWM methods. Additionally, the research uncovers a self-voltage recovery mechanism within the capacitor voltage that simplifies hardware implementation by requiring only steady-state voltage balancing. Simulated results validate the proposed component design method, demonstrating reductions in capacitance and enhancements in hardware control simplicity.

articleTitle: GaN-based Resonant Energy Transfer System for EV-Drives with Electrical Excitation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper presents a contactless energy transfer system for supplying the rotor of an electrically excited synchronous machine using gallium nitride as a wide-bandgap semiconductor material. Due to the requirements for maximum efficiency, a resonant LLC circuit topology is used. The design of the rotating high-frequency transformer with regard to optimal switching of the GaN semiconductors and the corresponding effects on the resonant circuit are discussed in detail in the paper. The operating behavior is evaluated by simulation and measurement of a test arrangement.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning Based Energy Management System to Maximize Efficiency for the Hybrid Marine Propulsion System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Hybrid maritime power typically employs energy management technologies such as rule-based or reactive control. The general purpose of this project is to investigate energy management and control approaches for hybrid marine boats using Reinforcement Learning (RL). This project aims to explore the potential of using online adaptive approaches to replace traditional energy management tactics. The initial study focused on a straightforward hybrid maritime power system. A Markov Decision Framework Q-Learning – RL algorithm was used to design a decision-making process. Integrated power systems, combining fuel cells and batteries, present a promising solution for marine propulsion systems, offering high energy density and power while reducing CO 2 emissions, aligning with the International Maritime Organization's goal of achieving net zero emissions by 2050. This study focuses on the implementation of fuel cell and battery systems, a dc-to-dc converter, typically a boost converter, to manage power flow between the fuel cell and battery, enhancing peak power output at propeller where induction machine utilized as a primary mover in a hybrid powertrain system. Using modeling and analysis, this research investigates power distribution scenarios based on varying power demands within onboard marine propulsion systems. Reinforcement Learning is employed to assess the State of Charge (SOC) of the battery and fuel cell density, optimizing power flow under different operational states to maximize total rewards and overall system efficiency. This study contributes to the advancement of marine propulsion systems by integrating Reinforcement learning control mechanisms to optimize power distribution.

articleTitle: Experimental Identification of the Inrush Safety Regions in Single-Phase Power Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper investigates the inrush current phenomenon in single-phase power transformers. A suitable experimental setup is designed to identify the locus of the point in the Br <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-\theta_{0}$</tex>plane, called the Inrush Safety Region (ISR), where the inrush current phenomenon does not occur. In particular, it is verified that, for a fixed value of Br, an Inrush Safety Angle Range exists in which the transient current value is comparable with its value in the steady state. This means that, in order to avoid the occurrence of the inrush current phenomenon, it is necessary that the operating point belongs to the ISR. From the above experimental results, it is expected that new inrush current control methods will be developed.

articleTitle: Introducing the Port Electric Distribution Network Concept
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: In view of extensive electrification of ports in an attempt to attain sustainability, in this paper, an effort is made to briefly outline the specificities of the configurations of the port distributions networks highlighting the issues that need to be carefully considered at both the design and operation stage. Moreover, a novel and rather advantageous approach of designing port networks is presented. It resembles the zonal configurations of ship networks blending in the smart micro grid concept, too.

articleTitle: Real-Time Hardware in the Loop Simulation Setup for Automotive Grid Interfacing System Based on PLECS RT BOX and National Instruments PXI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: In this paper, a novel Hardware in the Loop (HIL) simulation setup will be presented based on PLECS RT BOX I and NI PXIe-1071 Real-Time target computer. The software suite used for programming and management of the control unit (PXIe-1071) is based on NI VeriStand and MathWorks Matlab - Simulink. Within NI VeriStand the Simulink model will be associated with the physical I/O ports of the PXIe-1071 controller. The NI PXIe-1071 simulation computer can act both as HIL simulator or RCP simulator (Rapid Control Prototyping platform). The HIL software management and programming suite used for the RT BOX is PLECS Plexim which is a Power Electronics dedicated modeling and simulation environment. The whole setup will be able to simulate fast-switching power electronics topologies that are used in electric vehicle and smart grid interfacing with the associated control law and switching pattern strategies, helping the end user to find the appropriate parameters for the control law. Using the proposed setup, the energy flow of the EV battery charging unit can be simulated in real-time.

articleTitle: Design-Method of a High Power Eddy Current Brake as a Retarder for Electric Trucks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to braking in electric vehicles by integrating an eddy current brake (ECB) with an anisotropic material structure into the electric drive system as a retarder. Traditional regenerative braking methods, while effective, often require the battery to be undercharged to reserve capacity for braking energy, or the addition of a braking resistor, which increases system weight. The proposed ECB method offers a promising alternative by potentially reducing mechanical brake size, eliminating the need for a brake resistor, and allowing the battery to maintain a higher state of charge. It utilizes an anisotropic material structure within the ECB to enhance power density and improve heat distribution, thereby overcoming the typical limitations of lower power density in standard ECBs. This approach also aligns with the UN-ECE-13 directive for continuous braking function by effectively managing the braking energy without the typical drawbacks. The analysis includes optimization algorithms to determine the optimal size of the ECB under emergency braking conditions and continuous downhill scenarios, ensuring compliance with safety standards while enhancing vehicle efficiency and performance.

articleTitle: Influence of Current Sensor Faults on the Performances of Surface Mounted Permanent Magnet Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The current sensor faults have a great impact on the performance of the electrical drives used for propulsion and traction applications. This work analyzes the effects of the faults on the motor losses using a mathematical model of the current faults in the case of a permanent magnet electrical drives controlled with Field Oriented Control. In particular, the current sensor faults increase the total harmonic distortion of the phase currents with an impact on torque ripple, Joule and iron losses. The analysis is entirely carried out using an analytical approach for the torque ripple and finite element analysis for the losses. The results of different case studies for two surface mounted permanent magnet synchronous motors are reported and analyzed.

articleTitle: Double Stator Axial Airgap Spoke-PMSM Performance Investigation for High Torque Density by 3D FEM with a Direct-Drive Powertrain Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: High torque density together with high Nm/watt of copper loss and Nm/kg of sintered PM are paramount in EV(HEV) applications. In general values in the range of 60–80 Nm/l, 8–12 Nm/kg (of active volume and weight) and current densities for peak torque up to 20 A/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 100–120 Nm/kg of PM are obtained in the main commercial EV of today. Going above 200 Nm/l and above 200 Nm/kg of sintered PM is now in the R&D trends but still only up to 17 Nm/kg (active weight) have been in general reported recently. Building on previous recent work, the authors extend it by investigating the performance of a dual-stator spoke-PM Axial Flux PMSM drive for EVs by 2D/3D FEM. In this paper more than 230 Nm/l, 28 Nm/kg of active weight and more than 280 Nm/kg of sintered PM is demonstrated by 3D FEM for a case study of a 24 slots/32 poles rotor with 276 mm stator core diameter and 50 mm long stator stack for a current density of 22 A/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>•

articleTitle: PPL Integration Employing SMES System on Naval Vessel: Modeling and Co-Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Pulsed Power Loads integration is a challenging topic in the naval industry. To meet military standard and STANAG requirements, the implementation of energy storage systems is a promising solution. In this paper, the exploitation of a superconductive magnetic energy storage system to mitigate the effect of pulsed power load is investigated. A notional shipboard power system model, including four generators and a dc pulsed power load, is implemented in DIgSILENT PowerFactory. A detailed Electromagnetic Transient Model of a superconductive magnetic energy storage system is modeled in MATLAB Simulink. A control strategy is proposed and implemented, then the co-simulation of the two models is exploited of Functional Mock-up Interface. The simulation results show how the storage system minimizes the impact of the pulsed power load on the shipboard power system.

articleTitle: Implementation and Preliminary Testing of 26 kW Induction Machine in an Electric Traction System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper shows the construction and the preliminary test towards to an electric traction system with a 26kW induction machine as a laboratory test-bench setup. Through the bus CAN communication protocol is intended to obtain the mechanical and electrical parameters of the induction machine, these parameters can also be observed and evaluated in a touchscreen display for comfortable viewing. The system is featured by a liquid cold plate, a water pump and the radiator in order to keep cooled the whole traction system.

articleTitle: Load Profile Estimation for Electric Power Load Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: With the recent growth of All-Electric ships, estimating the total electric power load has become increasingly important. Modern shipboard power system configurations are incorporating energy storage systems to enhance efficiency, creating challenges in sizing the generation stations due to their time-dependent nature. Accurate power profiles are essential for sizing, management strategies, and estimating ship operations. In particular, the necessity to have a more accurate load profile is more and more essential for vessel with storage systems. To address the need for electric power profile estimation for ships, in this paper, we present a method to estimate the power profile of ship loads based on deterministic Electric Power Load Analysis (EPLA) integrated with a Markov chain model. This method is applied to shipboard power system design and validated through comparison with field measurements.

articleTitle: Toward Zero-Emissions Construction Sites: Mobile Battery Energy Storage Units Charged from the Regenerative Braking Energy of Traction Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Zero-emissions construction sites are a key part of the energy transition. Their energy supply can be ensured by mobile battery energy storage units as is currently being commercialized. However, the charging of these batteries is still limited by the grid congestion and the existence of a suitable charging infrastructure. Meanwhile, traction grids are notoriously underutilized high-power infrastructures with a significant amount of regenerative braking energy that is predominately wasted as heat in braking resistors. This paper suggests charging the construction sites-destined mobile batteries from the traction grids to harvest their otherwisewasted braking energy and relieve the congested distribution grid. The paper examines 7 different charging schemes for different battery sizes in four case studies of low- and hightraffic metro and trolleybus grids in Amsterdam and Arnhem, respectively. It is found that up to 88% of the battery charging can come from the otherwise-wasted braking energy.

articleTitle: Optimal Sizing of a Multi - Energy Port with Vehicles Charging Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This work proposes a three-stage optimal sizing procedure for a green smart port, considering boats and cars connected to the grid. A mixed integer linear programming formulation is exploited, integrating the operational profile of all the vehicles connected to the charging points. The aggregated power profile of all the vehicles is obtained through several iterations of the sizing algorithm. Electric vehicles can operate in vehicle-to-grid mode, performing energy regulation in order to maximize the port earnings. The algorithm, developed in the Matlab environment, is tested on a notional marina. The results demonstrate that the integration of the vehicles into the port can reduce the size of the storage system, especially when operating in vehicle-to-grid mode.

articleTitle: Reliability Assessment of Power Modules Across Mission Phases in Electric Aircraft Propulsion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The advancement in the development of high power density power converters is a major contributor towards electrified aircraft. Wide-bandgap power modules can drive this technology transition, yet ensuring reliability in the demanding aviation environment during early development is crucial. Balancing challenges such as high neutron flux and low-pressure environment-induced stress with high power density and low failure rates poses significant design challenges for power converter design. This paper evaluates failure rates of power modules for power converters in aircraft environments. The impact of junction temperature, voltage derating, and mission profile on reliability is assessed. Furthermore, an approach for a statistical failure rate assessment of SiC power modules during different phases of the flight is introduced.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control Applied to Hybridised Modular Fuel Cell Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper proposes a predictive control strategy to minimize the hydrogen consumption of a modular fuel cell system hybridized with a battery. This approach is compared with a reference solution obtained using optimal control. By increasing the prediction horizon, performances tends to the reference ones, minimizing the consumption and aging of the modules while maintaining a solution that can be implemented online. It is shown that the gains in energy consumption and module aging are achieved at the expense of battery aging in both cases.

articleTitle: Sensorless Start-Up Synchronization of Multi-3-Phase Segmented PMSM for Electrical Aircraft Propulsion Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Multi-3-phase PMSM with isolated inverters and controls per 3-phase machine segment are beneficial for electric aviation, providing redundancy and segregation. Partial operation of machine segments can further be utilized for efficiency optimization. Thus, synchronization techniques are required for the re-startup of machine segments, and re-synchronization to the rotation machine. This work proposes a technique for sensorless non-intrusive segment synchronization of segmented multi-3-phase PMSM. A sensorless, non-intrusive and signal-less synchronization using BEMF measurement and an SMO input signal switchover is implemented and validated using a pHiL test setup for up to six 3-phase machine segments.

articleTitle: A Potential 15 KVdc Catenary-Fed Rail Induction Motor Drive at 780 kW, 1.5-3 krpm: Preliminary Design and Key Fem Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Apart from the three types of rail power supplies in use <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-16.66 ~\text{Hz}, 15 \text{kV}$</tex> single phase a.c., <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50(60) \text{Hz}, 25$</tex> (27) kV single phase a.c. and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.5-3 \text{kVdc}$</tex> we hereby suggest, for interurban trains a 15 kVdc power supply in order to increase performance and reduce initial power electronics costs. In essence a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$132 \text{kV}-15 \text{kV} 3$</tex> phase transformer and a fully controlled rectifier will directly supply the 15 kVdc catenary on ground to reduce power electronics costs while solving the existent input a.c. phase asymmetries, harmonics at unity input power factor. On the vehicle 1 (or multiple) voltage self-boosting inverter supplied directly from the 15 kVdc an induction motors for traction in units at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$780 ~\text{kW}, 1.5-3 \text{krpm}$</tex> are suggested, while for auxiliary a 15 kVdc to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$500 / 300 \text{Vdc}$</tex> insulated d.c.-d.c. converter is suggested. The present paper presents the above suggested scheme and the preliminary electromagnetic design of the proposed 780 kW, 1.5-3 krpm induction motor for traction with key FEM validation. Developments on the proposed system will be approached in subsequent papers.

articleTitle: State-Space Modeling of Protection Circuits for Electronic Fuses in Vehicular Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Zonal low-voltage vehicular power system archi-tectures with electronic power distributors are currently being researched. These distributors contain electronic fuses that inter-connect the power supply with loads such as steering or brake actuators. In this paper, methods for the design and evaluation of protection circuits for these electronic fuses are presented. A state-space based approach separates nonlinear system dynamics into multiple linear conduction modes. This method allows a resource-saving calculation of stress on electronic components, analyses of sensitivities and novel trigger mechanisms. The introduced multi stage first order model of the electronic fuse achieves a deviation of less than 5 % compared to the validated exponential first order fuse model. The method is verified by means of three state-of-the-art protection circuits.

articleTitle: Energy Management Algorithm for an Advanced EV Fast-Charging System with Bipolar DC-link, Energy Storage and Photovoltaics Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This article investigates an energy management algorithm for an advanced electric vehicle (EV) fast charging system with supplementary battery energy storage and photo-voltaics (PV) integration. The considered system is founded on a bipolar, three-wire DC-link for improved flexibility and ensures bidirectional power flow for the converters in order to support a myriad of operating modes. The system consists of a grid converter, isolated dc-dc converters for slow and fast vehicle charging, and non-isolated dc-dc converters: one interfacing the energy storage and another for the PV system. Given the wide possibilities for the operation of the system, an intricate flowchart-based algorithm is proposed for the control of the system. Finally, some of the operation modes are analyzed in detail and further validated using the experimental in-house built model, with the scaled system rated at 1500 V and with a power of up to 20 kW per single converter.

articleTitle: Infrastructure and Battery Capacity Impact on BEMU's Battery Lifetime
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The autonomy of battery trains, about 80km today, is too short for 50% of the journey trips in France. Two options could be envisaged to increase the relevant area of battery trains, the partial electrification or increase the specific energy of the batteries. Each choice will have an impact on the battery's lifetime, train operation and battery train economical model. This paper quantifies their impact on the battery lifetime.

articleTitle: Optimal Energy Management of FC- Battery Shipboard Power System using Dynamic Programming
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The move towards more sustainable shipping has increased interest in using fuel cell-battery hybrid power systems. The sector still lacks know-how on the optimal energy management in such a design. Two key performance indices are the fuel consumption and FC degradation, which are conflicting objectives for the optimization. Offline optimization of energy management with a known power profile is a useful tool for determining control approaches and providing a benchmark for the performance of real-time control implementations. This work solves the optimization problem of the power split between fuel cells and energy storage systems by quantizing the timestate space and finding the optimal trajectory via dynamic programming. The optimization additionally allows for the on-off switching of fuel cell modules as an additional degree of freedom in the presence of multiple fuel cell modules integrated into the shipboard power system. The optimal trajectories for multiple FC modules and the ESS are computed for a given load profile. Results indicate that the FC degradation can be significantly reduced by optimizing the timing of on- and off-switching. The selective switching of modules further increases the widens the Pareto-optimal front curve's span of optimal combinations of fuel consumption and FC degradation.

articleTitle: Research on Parallel Control Method for More Electric Aircraft High Voltage DC Electric Power System Considering Line Impedance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: In order to address the uneven current distribution caused by the difference of line impedance in parallel electric power system (EPS) and the bus voltage drop in traditional droop control, this paper proposes an improved droop control strategy that considering the line impedance. Firstly, the influence of line impedance on current distribution accuracy is analyzed. Subsequently, the line impedance is taken into account in the droop coefficient to achieve equal current distribution. On this basis, a voltage compensation link is added to compensate for the busbar voltage drop caused by the initial droop coefficient. Finally, to verify the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy, a simulation model of a 3 -stage generator high voltage DC (HVDC) parallel EPS was established, and the simulation results of three control methods are compared. The results show that the control strategy proposed in this paper can improve the defects of traditional control method, while also achieving both bus voltage regulation and average current distribution.

articleTitle: A Methodology to Assess the Sustainability of E-motors in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Road transport is the UK's largest contributor to greenhouse gas emissions, accounting for approximately 24% of total gas emissions in 2020. Therefore, a transition to more sustainable road transport is needed and electric vehicles are key to this transition. However, a truly sustainable solution must go beyond simply considering a reduction in greenhouse gas emissions and considering the full circular economy of the electric vehicle, including electric vehicle systems, sub-systems and equipment. A further challenge is that the sustainability of these systems must be balanced with meeting performance criteria, including weight. A life cycle mapping is showcased to understand the end-of-life scenarios of subcomponents in the electric motor. The methodology created in this paper will include a ranking system based on the current design of Protean electric motor. It will also include a scope of improvement in subcomponents and an effort - impact score which is determined based on the possible solutions to identify opportunities for sustainable electric motor design.

articleTitle: A Distributed Simulation of Electrical Machines on FPGAs Using Low Latency Communication Protocol
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Due to their high switching frequencies, real-time simulations with short frame times are essential for simulating power electronics systems. While Modern Digital Real-time Simulation (DRTS) platforms offer off-the-shelf simulation resources, they require significant cost. In this research, we present a low-cost, high-performance simulation approach that can be utilized to simulate large power electronics systems in real- time. We use a modular programming approach to partition and test the simulated model into two Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs). We developed a communication module based on existing link-layer protocols optimized for lower latency and high bandwidth to meet real-time timing requirements.

articleTitle: Estimating Cost Benefit of Supply-Demand Adjustment Utilizing Railway Onboard Batteries Based on Their Deterioration Test
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: It is important to make more effective use of large onboard batteries for railway decarbonization. In this work, we conducted cyclic tests of onboard LIBs for driving: power assisting and regenerative absorption, as well as a combined case of participating in supply-demand adjustment. The cyclic test results suggest that there is a battery-specific SOC range where charge-discharge cycles for driving should be avoided. We also estimate the economical supply-demand adjustment conditions of charge-discharge amount, based on their deterioration test result while avoiding excessive battery deterioration.

articleTitle: Evaluation of a Dual MLC2 Converter for Electrified Ship Propulsion Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
