abstract: In this work, a performance analysis on the application of the modular five-level multilevel clamped multilevel converter (5L-MLC2) for driving high-power machine, commonly used in naval plants for propulsion, is presented. Focus is on the topology using dual multilevel converters connected to induction motors with open terminals (open-end windings), that is, each end of the windings is connected to an inverter. The viability of this configuration is verified in this work. A comparison analysis is performed between the modular five-level multilevel clamped multilevel converter (5L-MLC2), and the well-known three-level neutral-point-clamped converter (3L-NPC). The strategy of applying phase shifted modulating signals between the converters, either with S-PWM or SVM, have been considered. Performance analysis with Matlab/Simulink was carried out with emphasis on FFT analysis and current and voltage levels on the semiconductor devices. Some results have shown reduced total harmonic distortion (THD%) at 120° phase shift with SVM. The proposed dual 5L-MLC2 based drive system has yielded significant reduction in total rated voltage of clamping diodes.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Battery-Internal-Heating Method Involving Dq-Axis Current Pulsation in Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors During Electric Vehicle Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The discharge voltage and capacity of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), widely used in electric vehicles (EVs), decrease at sub-zero temperatures. Therefore, the temperature needs to be rapidly increased to increase the output of the drive motor. One of the methods for raising the internal temperature of LIBs is the usage of the Joule heat of LIBs. A method for raising the internal temperature during EV operation has been developed by pulsating the dq-axis current of a permanent magnet synchronous motor on an equal-torque curve and generating Joule heat in the battery via alternating current. In this study, the quantitative relationship between the frequency and amplitude of the dq-axis current pulsation and the battery current is established and the mechanism of the temperatureraising method is clarified. The effect of the heating method involving dq-axis current pulsation is also clarified quantitatively to design the drive system.

articleTitle: Optimisation Models for the Location of Refuelling Stations for Fuel Cell Electric Freight Vehicles in Italy: Preliminary Tests
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper proposes possible approaches to the optimal location of refuelling stations for hydrogen vehicles. The study originates from a proposal in Italy, within the framework of the Recovery and Resilience Plan, to install 40 refuelling stations on the main road network to promote the use of hydrogen-powered vehicles for freight transport. As the number of stations is very limited compared to the extent of the road network, they need to be very well located to intercept flows as much as possible. This paper proposes two models based on identifying road links to place the facility: one maximises the demand served, while the other maximises the number of origin-destination pairs covered. These models were tested with a heuristic algorithm on a test network that schematically reproduces part of the Italian national network.

articleTitle: Online Broadband Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy within Direct Power Control of a Neutral Point Clamped Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This article proposes a new method for online electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) of batteries using a modified direct power controlled (DPC) grid-connected three-phase neutral point clamped (NPC) inverter. The method stimulates the battery by applying a pseudo-random binary sequence (PRBS) EIS signal to the dc link-capacitor voltage balancing control loop of the inverter. The proposed approach has been verified using a grid-connected NPC inverter model in MATLAB/Simulink. The method enables online battery diagnosis and management without the need for ancillary electronic circuits.

articleTitle: Preliminary Methodologies for Selecting Diesel Railways to Be Converted to Hydrogen
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Although rail transport is often considered a crucial component of sustainable mobility, in some cases, such as non-electrified railway lines using diesel trains, it may not be entirely sustainable. The ideal solution would be to electrify these lines, but low demand and/or low traffic do not justify the costs relating to the installation of the contact line, the construction of electrical substations and the complete replacement of the train fleet. In this context, the conversion of non-electrified lines from diesel to hydrogen could be a suitable compromise. Indeed, in this context, the Italian National Recovery and Resilience Plan includes investment in hydrogen experimentation on railways and requires the identification of lines to be converted to hydrogen. Hence, this paper proposes some methodologies for identifying the lines suitable for conversion.

articleTitle: A Position Sensorless Startup Method for DSEM Based on Pulse Injection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper proposes a startup method for doubly salient electro-magnetic motor (DSEM) based on H-bridge converter. Firstly, the influence between three-phase currents and excitation current under the drive of H-bridge converter is analyzed. Then, a pulse injection-based method is proposed to estimate the position during the startup process by comparing the magnitude of the response current. This method fully utilizes the falling edge of the acceleration pulse, with only one test pulse injected to obtain the self-inductance relationship, it reduces the number of test pulse injections, thus improving the startup performance. Moreover, this method avoids the influence between three-phase currents and excitation current, and it does not depend on the accuracy of the previous position estimation. The injected test current does not generate negative torque. Finally, the feasibility and correctness of this method are verified through an 18/12 pole DSEM experimental platform.

articleTitle: Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer Optimization Using Adaptative Termination in Center-Fed Resonant Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Conventional Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) systems, with a single coil transmitter, used in automotive applications, have a high cost-to-energy transfer ratio as consequence of the short range and high number of power components required, making them a costly solution to implement. The utilization of a resonant array as the transmitter significantly extends the distance and time frame during which energy is transferred to the receiver, with minimal cost increase. Furthermore, the power transmission, range, and energy transfer can be improved through a centerfed resonant array. However, a consequence of this solution is the need for a termination resistance at both ends of the array, whose value affects the performance and behavior of the system. In this work, an adaptative termination and control strategy on both ends of the array is proposed so that the energy transfer between transmitter and receiver can be maximized, taking full advantage of a center-fed array used in dynamic WPT systems aimed at automotive applications.

articleTitle: Electric Propulsion System with Hybrid Powertrain Equipped with Diesel/Gas Generators and Battery-Buffered AC Common Bus for LNG Ships
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: In the contemporary maritime industry, energy-efficient operations on ships are increasingly prevalent, motivated by mandatory regulations from sector-leading organizations aimed at reducing carbon emissions. Electric propulsion systems are an alternative solution to further enhance energy efficiency by ensuring optimum power flow between alternative sources and common busbars. This study presents an electric propulsion system with hybrid powertrain for an LNG ship and its power management system. The powertrain is composed of a common AC busbar, diesel generator, LNG generator, battery, and electric motors. The relevant system has the advantages of having an energy storage system to supply critical loads under challenging conditions and prioritizing the use of LNG instead of diesel generators, thereby reducing COx emissions. Additionally, it encompasses synchronization challenges brought about by the use of multiple power sources. The synchronization of these diesel and LNG generators to the battery-buffered common AC bus presents its own challenging issues. In this study, both the energy-efficient electric propulsion system layout and the power management system that ensures low-emission and efficient system operation have been described.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of Aircraft Power Systems Based on Transients and Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Aerospace power systems are largely equipped with electrical circuits and electronic subsystems and components. Faults occurring within aircraft or spacecraft electrical systems may potentially put at risk the safety of the flight. This work presents a new approach based on transients caused by electrical failures and deep learning architectures to identify and diagnose faults of different components and subsystems within a conventional aircraft power system. The electrical components and subsystems to be diagnosed include: the power generation unit, primary and secondary electric distribution subsystems, transformer and rectifier units (TRU), the busbars that provide power to the bank of DC/AC loads that include motors which serve as actuators and resistive loads such as lamps or light bulbs. Two deep learning architectures were investigated: one based on LSTM neural networks and the other one based on one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D-CNN). Classification accuracies of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{9 6. 0 9 \%}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{9 5. 5 4 \%}$</tex> were obtained with LSTM neural networks for the training and testing sets, respectively.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Energy Management of Urban-Rail-Transit-based Micro Grid Integrated with EV
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The electric vehicle charging station (EVCS) has been widely constructed in urban areas, especially aside by urban railway transit (URT). This trend forms a novel energy integration of URT-based micro grid (URT-MG) with EVCS. To economically manage the energy flow of the URT-MG with EVCS, this research proposes a two-stage energy management, considering the substation operation cost and stability. First, a control strategy of URT-MG is proposed which can reduce the substation peak power. Then, a day-ahead energy management method is designed to reduce the system operation cost, based the forecast RES power and EV behaviour. In the second stage, a smart charging strategy of EVCS is proposed to meet the EV customer's travel demand in the actual operation. The proposed method is verified by simulation based on Merseyrail line in Liverpool, and the energy cost of traction substation is reduced by 23.4%.

articleTitle: 150 kVA Compact Modular Three-Level NPC Auxiliary Converter for the Railways Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper introduces a compact and modular three-level Neutral Point Clamped (3L-NPC) DC-DC converter designed for auxiliary inverters used in Railways. Compared to traditional topologies employing 50 Hz transformers, the 3L-NPC dual active bridge (DAB) DC-DC converters, with integrated high-frequency transformers, offer modularity, compactness, and higher power density. The proposed design enables independent control for each converter, facilitating parallel feeding of AC loads (such as fans, blowers, and pumps), with the second converter dedicated to charging 110 V batteries. The proposed topology, along with its control system, is simulated using PLECS and validated through hardware-in-loop setups under various load conditions. Additionally, the power-density of the 3L-NPC dual active bridge DC-DC converters is demonstrated to surpass that of conventional auxiliary converters while being more adaptable to scalability for higher power applications. These findings confirm the converter's simplicity, ease of operation, and potential for future power scalability.

articleTitle: Dispatchable Battery Swapping System with Centralized Charging and Renewable Energy Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The effort to electrify society has in recent years resulted in major changes in the transportation sector. Charging time remains a challenge in several applications such as transportation and heavy machinery. A proposed solution that shortens the energy replenishment time and adds flexibility in loading the grid is to battery-swapping: exchanging the depleted battery for a fully charged one. In some cases, it can be beneficial to perform the battery-swapping operations at a separate location from where charging infrastructure is available, for example, in heavy machinery systems or remote road swapping stations. This paper presents a genetic algorithm that can plan and evaluate the logistics and charging behavior of such a system. A case study is conducted and the effect of key system characteristics such as available battery stock and transportation distance is analyzed.

articleTitle: Exploration of Partial Power Converter Topology for Fuel Cell Multi-Stack Systems in Heavy-Duty Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The Partial Power Converter (PPC) is a very appealing solution for DC/DC applications because of its inherent merits in terms of efficiency, power density and system redundancy. In this paper, we explore the use of PPC topology for Heavy-Duty Fuel Cell Electric Vehicles, in a Multi-Stack configuration. A Series-Cascade connected reconfigurable converter, based on a phase-shifted full bridge converter is proposed. Theoretical analysis and simulation of the proposed converter show its feasibility. An evaluation of the proposed converter's performance over a long haul driving cycle concludes the work.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Current Limiting Control Strategy for DC Solid-State Power Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper proposes a two-stage current limiting control strategy for DC Solid-State Power Controllers (SSPCs), aimed at addressing the challenges posed by inrush current and thermal stress during the rapid switching of large capacitive loads. In the resistor-based current limiting stage, a current-limiting resistor is utilized to suppress the inrush current, thereby protecting the system from instantaneous high current damage. In the gate voltage clamping current limiting stage, the gate voltage of the main-branch MOSFET is clamped to a given value, enabling rapid charging of the load capacitor. Throughout the limiting process, natural commutation occurs between the main branch and the current-limiting branch, resulting in a continuous variation of the SSPC's equivalent resistance. This effectively reduces secondary inrush current and fully utilizes the thermal capacity of the power devices. Experimental results show that the SSPC employing this strategy can switch on a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3300\mu \mathrm{F}$</tex> capacitive load within 10.1ms, with an initial inrush current of 191A and a secondary inrush current of less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$76\mathrm{A}$</tex>, verifying the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Decoupled Levitation and Propulsion Control of Single-Sided Linear Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This article describes a simultaneous and decoupled scheme for the control of levitation and propulsion forces of single-sided linear induction motors (SLIMs). The proposed control scheme utilizes a highly accurate SLIM analytical model to ensure the operation of the motor at the best efficiency point while achieving lift and thrust forces decoupling through a multi-frequency supply strategy adapted from the literature. The described control scheme has been implemented and validated in MATLAB Simulink.

articleTitle: An Empirical Model for State of Charge Estimation Based on Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) is an accurate method used to study the internal properties of lithium-ion (Li-ion) battery cells. It is important to accurately estimate the State of Charge (SoC) of Li-ion battery cells for safety and longevity considerations. There are several methods to estimate the SoC; however, accurate methods require a lot of computational resources and increase the system complexity. This paper proposes an EIS-based experimental method for SoC estimation based on calculating the area under the EIS magnitude vs. frequency curve and correlating the result with SoC. The results demonstrate a relationship between the EIS magnitude and the SoCs within a certain range and under specific conditions. Furthermore, the suggested method reduces the errors and eliminates the need for fitting the EIS impedance spectrum for SoC estimation.

articleTitle: Common Mode Voltage Suppression Strategy for Third-Harmonic Injection Two-Stage Matrix Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: In response to the problem of high amplitude common mode voltage (CMV) in the third harmonic injection two-stage matrix converter (3TSMC), the CMV suppression methods of active zero state PWM (AZSPWM) and near-state PWM (NSPWM) are applied to 3TSMC, which reduced the voltage amplitude of the CMV without increasing hardware. Firstly, the expression for the CMV of 3TSMC is derived, and then the suppression principle of the improved modulation algorithm is analyzed. Then, the influence of dead zone effect on the method is considered and the dead zone is compensated. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through experiments.

articleTitle: Swift Quasi-Peak Detector Implementation using Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper presents an Python implementation of a CISPR 16-1-1 time-domain EMI receiver for post-processing of transient data originating from circuit simulation or oscilloscope measurement. The scientific novelty is the implementation of the Quasi-Peak (QP) detector with the help of machine learning (ML). The QP ML-model is trained with an automated lab-oratory setup using an actual EMI receiver and parameterized impulse burst train stimuli. The advantage of the proposed model is that it can very quickly and accurately predict QP readings from only one period of transient input data. In contrast, classic QP detector implementations require a waveform input of at least 2 seconds and a model of the critically damped meter to evaluate the settled QP reading.

articleTitle: The Present Status of the Extremely High-Power Charging Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Heavy-duty electric vehicles (HDEVs) are becoming more common globally. The battery capacities in these vehicles are also increasing, so charging with extremely high power is needed for convenient usage. This paper presents an overview of the highpower chargers that have appeared in literature. The rated power of the chargers ranges from 350 kW to 4.5 MW. The main scope is in the AC-DC and DC-DC converters, and what type of topologies have been implemented. Other points of interest are the use of SiC MOSFETs and the overall efficiency of the system.

articleTitle: Configuration Research of the Multi-Mode Hybrid Electric Vehicles with Two Electric Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: There are many types of Hybrid Electric Vehicles (HEVs) with two electric machines (EMs) on the market. These powertrains with two EMs is conducive to increasing the operating modes, however, the multiple operating modes are very significant to improving the vehicle dynamics and fuel economy. In order to explore the effect of multiple operating modes and multiple gears of HEVs with two EMs, this research based on the existing vehicle models (Toyota Prius, Honda Accord and Chevrolet Volt), and a powertrain system with multiple gears and multiple operating modes (named “Toyota MMMG”) of the Toyota Company to discuss their acceleration performance and fuel economy. This paper analyzed the acceleration performance of these hybrids at 0–120 km/h via a dynamic programming algorithm and used the Rapid dynamic programming (Rapid-DP) method to evaluate their fuel economy under the four driving cycles (FUDS, HWFET, NEDC, and WLTP). Finally, in order to overcome the drawback of the Toyota MMMG, a new configuration was proposed and discussed in this article. It improves acceleration by 53.9% relative to the Prius.

articleTitle: Extending Feasible Load-Independent Voltage Gain Range in Wireless Power Transfer Links
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Fixed-frequency constant-coupling series (capacitor) - series (capacitor) compensated inductive wireless power transfer links (SS(CC)-IWPTL) may be designed to operate with certain load independent voltage gain (LIVG), constrained by parameters of the loosely coupled transformer (LCT). Due to the fact that LCT parameters values are not arbitrary in practice, targeted LIVG value may not reside within attainable region. This may require for an additional power conversion stage, reducing power density and reliability of the system while increasing size and cost. This work reveals that employing an inductor instead of a capacitor as one of the two series compensation elements allows to extend the feasible LIVG range for given LCT parameters, followed by corresponding compensation elements sizing guidelines. The revealed methodology is validated by means of simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: An LLC-DAB Hybrid Converter With High Inputoutput Voltage Ratio Based on an Integrated Matrix Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The LLC-DAB hybrid topology attains voltage regulation capability, while the LLC operates at a resonant frequency for high efficiency. In applications featuring a high ratio of the input to output voltage, the series and parallel multiple transformers can effectively reduce the voltage and current stress of the transformer. However, the large quantity of transformer units and bulky magnetic components result in low power density and low efficiency. Therefore, the planar magnetic integrated matrix transformer is adopted to solve these problems. This article gives the operation principle of an LLC-DAB hybrid converter, and a six-leg integrated matrix transformer is designed for a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.5 ~\text{kW} 750 ~\mathrm{V} / 48 ~\mathrm{V}$</tex> LLC-DAB hybrid topology. Further optimization of the core based on loss is given. The decoupling conditions are given according to the simplified magnetic circuit model. A simulation model is built in ANSYS Maxwell software. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed matrix transformer structure.

articleTitle: Improvement of Utilizing Renewable Energy by Applying Stationary Energy Storage Systems in DC Traction Power Supply System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The installation of PV is spreading toward the realization of carbon neutrality in 2050. The power generation characteristic of PVs is significantly dependent on daylight, season and weather, and is different from those of conventional power sources. In contrast, daily power demand curve of railways is significantly different from the characteristic of PV power. Therefore, the significance of utilizing stationary energy storage systems for the demand control of PVs becomes larger. Firstly, the authors have proposed new charge/discharge characteristics of stationary energy storage systems for charging PV energy from power grid. Secondly, the authors have proposed integrated control of some stationary energy storage systems in the DC traction power supply system. The authors have carried out a study on effectiveness of the demand response (DR) control system for the energy storage systems. This DR control system charges or discharges to stationary energy storage systems in accordance with the power demand. The effectiveness of the proposed control system is confirmed by a train operation power simulator.

Author Keywords: DC traction power supply system (DC TPSS)

articleTitle: An Innovative Discrete-Time dq-Axis Model Considering Phase Discretization Error for High-Speed IM Drive and Its Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The field-oriented control (FOC)-based auto current regulators (ACRs) are commonly designed under the ideal assumption that the phase is obtained continuously when performing the Park transformation, but the current regulators are always discretely implemented. It will inevitably introduce non-negligible phase discretization errors with the increase of fundamental-to-switching(control) frequency ratio <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left(f_{e} / f_{s}\right)$</tex>. Therefore, an innovative discrete-time <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d q$</tex>-axis model for AC motor considering the Park transformation phase discretization error is proposed and the corresponding ACR is designed. Then, the decoupling performance and stability of the proposed closedloop current system are theoretically analyzed using complex vector method. Furthermore, the proposed discretization method is subsequently performed on an induction motor (IM) and verified through simulations and experiments. Eventually, the Padé approximant order of the discrete control matrix is discussed.

articleTitle: Integrated Digital Platform for Marine Energy Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Marine transportation plays a crucial role in global commerce, yet its environmental impact remains a concern. This paper proposes a draft architecture for a maritime digital platform, with a focus on optimizing ship energy systems to enhance sustainability. A key component of the proposed platform architecture is the integration of digital models with real-time data and predictive analytics, providing operators with valuable insights into energy consumption, battery health, and distribution management. By facilitating informed decision-making, the proposed platform aims to enhance system performance, durability, and environmental responsibility. Sensitive maritime data is protected through the implementation of advanced security protocols and encryption techniques, ensuring adherence to recognized industry cybersecurity standards. This paper introduces the fundamental components of the proposed digital platform, emphasizing its potential to revolutionize ship energy management and contribute to a more sustainable maritime industry.

articleTitle: State-of-Charge, State-of-Health and State-of-Power Estimation for Traction Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Nowadays, Lithium-ion batteries (Li-Ion) are employed in many high-power applications such as energy storage systems and electric vehicles. Therefore, to ensure they safe operation, Battery Management System (BMS) monitor the battery modules, avoiding failures and ensuring its expected lifetime through the evaluation of three indexes: state-of-charge (SoC), state-of-health (SoH) and state-of-power (SoP). For this purpose, it is necessary to have an accurate estimation of these indexes, which degrade over time both in relation to the use of the battery and the external environmental parameters. In this paper, a new hybrid approach is proposed to estimate SoC, SoH and SoP based on series resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r_{s}$</tex> and incremental capacitance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c$</tex> values of Thevenin battery model (TBM) used to describe the dynamic behavior of the battery. A multi-layer-perceptron (MLP) neural network is designed to estimate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r_{{s}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c$</tex> parameters of TBM. Finally, SoC, SoH and SoP are estimated by using a statistical approach. Numerical results and comparison analysis with the benchmark, show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Integrated Control Method for Stationary and Onboard Energy Storage Systems on DC Electrified Railway
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Recently, with the increasing installation of renewable energy sources such as photovoltaic (PV) power sources or wind farms, a so-called “demand response” (DR) to maintain the balance between supply and demand in the power grid has attracted attention. We propose an integrated control method for stationary energy storage systems (SESSs) and onboard energy storage systems (OESSs) on DC electrified railways to implement DR-based control. We confirmed the behavior of SESSs and OESSs in simulation when applying this control, and evaluated the difference in unit demand in 30 minutes between with and without the DR command.

articleTitle: Improved Charging Technique for Reducing the Charging Time in Nickel Manganese Cobalt Type Lithium-ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The charging time of the high-powered Lithiumion battery packs is one of the primary drawbacks of Electric vehicles. To this day, the charging protocol followed is the constant current and the constant voltage, where the battery initially charges in a constant current state and transitions to a constant voltage state when the battery voltage reaches peak value. This paper proposes a modified charging technique that effectively reduces the charging time by decreasing the time in a constant voltage state. This charging technique is applied on a 4.2V, 2.2Ah Nickel Manganese Cobalt battery in the laboratory setup. The results show a decrease in the charging time of 9.7% compared to the existing charging technique.

articleTitle: Railway Rolling Stocks' Long Parking Strategies for Energy Saving
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: In recent years, the energy crisis has even more encouraged the research on energy consumption reduction in railways. This process of optimization of the energy consumption has been engaged for a long time at SNCF Voyageurs (the main railway operator for passengers' transportation in France). Firstly, the studies were focused on energy savings during service, but it became noticeable that a large part of energy is spent during standstill (parking phase). In this paper, first a brief historical review of the applied parking strategies at SNCF Voyageurs will be presented. Followed by a detailed analysis of the current energy saving modes deployed on trains and their observed benefits. Finally, the future “panto down” strategy's operational challenges and technical constraints will be exposed along with its attractive energy savings.

articleTitle: Integrated Framework for Initial Position Estimation and Self-Commissioning of SRM Using Voltage Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Switched reluctance motors have gained popularity across various applications, including electric vehicles, owing to their advantages such as low manufacturing costs and the absence of rare-earth magnets. However, their highly nonlinear control characteristics present significant challenges. Given that torque generation in switched reluctance motors relies on precise rotor position knowledge, position estimation emerges as a crucial research area for these machines. While the conventional asymmetric half-bridge drive is widely employed, this study investigates an initial position estimation method utilizing a full-bridge bipolar drive, leveraging voltage signals exclusively. The method is explained and verified using finite element analysis data of an 8/6 switched reluctance motor. Findings demonstrate the feasibility of establishing an integrated framework for both initial position estimation and self-commissioning, capitalizing on the same information utilized for position estimation. The results are presented for several faults showing the effectiveness of the approach. Further developments might be applied for using the same approach for fault diagnosis or even fault tolerant control during motor running state in the next steps.

articleTitle: Analytical Approach to Define the Stability Boundaries in Controlled DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The DC technology is envisioned as the most promising alternative for the design of the new generation of shipboard power systems. The superior flexibility that the DC grids guarantee in respect to their AC counterpart make them the ideal candidate for the integration of demanding and high power loads. One of the components that make it possible to enhance the dynamics performance of such grids are definitely the power electronics converters. These fully controllable interfaces make it possible to easily coordinate the combination of generating sources, storages and loads, while guaranteeing adequate power quality. The price to pay for guaranteeing performing controls is the possibility to jeopardize the power system. Indeed, one of the risks of not properly controlled DC grids is the insurgence of voltage instability, an event that can possibly lead to a ship blackout. Considering systems with many converters the study of the voltage stability is not an easy task and certainly not doable with a full analytical approach. This is why this paper proposes a reduced-order approach for the problem to obtain a simplified analytical, yet approximated, expression of the system stability conditions.

articleTitle: Combined Control of a Segmented Stator Switched Reluctance Motor Drive for an Electric Motorcycle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The electric motorcycle is a focus of increasing interest in the electric vehicle market. Usually, electric motorcycles are propelled by powertrains using permanent magnet synchronous motor drives. This paper proposes a segmented stator-switched reluctance motor drive as an alternative. The main goal is to present a control system that ensures the powertrain's operation across all speeds. Additionally, it aims to reduce the size of the DC-link capacitor with a smooth torque with lower ripple, particularly at low speeds. The system will combine direct torque control in the lowspeed range and current chopping control or angle pulse control with variable turn-on and turn-off angles in the medium to high-speed range. Simulation results demonstrate the goodness of the proposal.

articleTitle: High-Side High-Voltage, Low-Current, and Temperature Sensor with Digital Interface for Electrospray Thrusters Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Recent advancements in electric propulsion have revolutionized related industries. Electrospray thrusters offer an alternative to traditional systems, potentially enabling wide adoption in small satellites due to electronics miniaturization. Electrospray thruster thrust correlates directly with emitted current. Maintaining a constant current by adjusting voltage ensures consistent thrust, underscoring the importance of monitoring thruster behavior. Furthermore, the sensor architecture can be configured to measure either the positive or negative rail with only changes to the wiring, requiring no additional modifications. This paper introduces a high-side sensor for kilovolt, microamp, and temperature measurements with a digital interface. Designed with automotive-grade components, it underwent a 7-hour validation test with electrospray thrusters.

articleTitle: Modeling and Control of a Direct Current Ferry Shipboard Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper presents a dynamic simulation model for a DC ferry shipboard power system utilizing Permanent Magnet-assisted Synchronous Reluctance Machine (PMSynRM) for the diesel genset and the propulsion systems. A battery storage system and advanced control strategies, were integrated with the model to ensure a stable DC bus voltage. Specifically, the battery storage supports the DC bus during rapid propulsion motor acceleration, by enhancing overall system performance and reliability. The study employs a comprehensive approach, including system-level configuration, dynamic modelling of primary components, and simulation case studies to evaluate system performance under various operational conditions. Results indicate that the integrated battery storage system and power control strategy effectively manage sudden power demands, ensuring stable operation of the common DC bus, while improving the overall performance and reliability of the ferry shipboard power system.

articleTitle: Efficiency Comparison of Full-Bridge DC-DC Converters for High-Power EV Charging Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Isolated full-bridge DC-DC converters are being extensively used when power levels of over 100 kWare needed for fast charging of electric vehicles. This paper analyses the efficiencies of two popular unidirectional converter topologies, namely phase-shift full-bridge converter and LLC converter that utilize silicon carbide semiconductors. Efficiencies of the converters at partial load and various input-output voltage levels are evaluated by by simulations in Plexim PLECS. The results show that the designed phase-shift full-bridge converter has higher efficiency than the LLC converter when high boost ratio is required, whereas the LLC converter has higher efficiency near the nominal operating voltages.

articleTitle: Systematic Approach to Design, Modeling and Characterization of Externally Excited Synchronous Machines for Traction Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: To evaluate the use of an externally excited synchronous machine (EESM) in electric vehicles, a thorough understanding of the machine's operating characteristics is essential. The influence of the high magnetic saturation, complex field distribution and cross-coupling effects should not be ignored when designing an EESM. The variation of the machine parameters, such as inductances, can affect the torque estimation and consequently the control accuracy. This paper deals with preliminary design and modeling of an EESM, highlighting the non-linear characteristics of the machine. Based on these characteristics, the set point current profiles are computed and an efficiency map is predicted.

articleTitle: Cost Analysis of Megawatt Charging and Overnight Charging for Battery Long-Haul Trucks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The timely installation and economical operation of public charging infrastructure along the main transport routes is of paramount importance for the market rollout of battery long-haul trucks. It is of the utmost urgency that the installation and operation of charging infrastructure for megawatt systems and overnight charging for battery long-haul trucks be realised at acceptable costs. In order to provide planners and operators of charging infrastructure with a better understanding of the costs and possible effects, a total cost of ownership for public charging infrastructure has been developed. The model analyses the correlations between charging infrastructure and grid connection costs as well as charging demand and service quality based on location-specific utilisation in order to demonstrate the effects on the resulting charging price. The economic analysis indicates that high utilisation rates are necessary, particularly for the Megawatt Charging System, in order to achieve low charging prices. However, only low site utilisation rates can be expected in the initial phase due to a lack of market penetration.

articleTitle: Centralized Diagnosis of On-Board Power Supply Network Faults with LSTM-Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Electronic systems in automobiles for highly automated driving functions must be significantly more reliable than today. Improved diagnosis can help to archive this goal. Nowadays, electronic systems have implemented some diagnosis functions which refer to the functionality of the component based on the voltage at the input terminals. Faults in a vehicle power supply systems are often only detected by the systems when voltage levels are out of range. Advanced fault detection methods for the supply system that can identify a root cause or a fault location were not known. In this paper, a new diagnosis concept for the overall power supply system is proposed. A centralized diagnosis concept which could be implemented in a power supply distribution unit (PDU) consisting of electronic fuses is presented. By evaluating the current and voltage signals in the PDU, typical on-board power supply system faults can be classified and localized. The diagnosis approach is based on the training of an artificial intelligence model with simulation data. The trained model is then applied to real measurements in a laboratory setup. The results show good fault detection accuracy and short detection times of 50<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mu}$</tex>s for the investigated cases in a laboratory setup.

articleTitle: Optimal Current Control of Switched Reluctance Motors Over the Entire Operating Range
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Controlling Switched Reluctance Motors (SRMs) requires careful selection of conduction angles to ensure optimal performance under various operating conditions. At low speeds, hysteresis control can provide the required torque by selecting the appropriate current reference. However, torque quality and efficiency can be further improved by selecting the right conduction angles. In contrast, conduction angles are the only control parameters at high speeds since peak current control is impossible. Hence, choosing the right conduction angles can significantly impact the average torque, torque ripple, and the RMS value of phase current, loss, and efficiency. This paper discusses the effects of turn-on and turn-off angles on average torque, torque ripple, and Integral Time Absolute Error (ITAE). Genetic Algorithm (GA) is used to find optimized firing angles, and the objective function for optimization is maximizing the average torque. The paper proposes a comprehensive approach to automatically control the conduction angles that excite SRMs at variable speeds, reference currents, and DC-link voltages. The results of the simulation demonstrate the efficacy of this method. Furthermore, the proposed controls are evaluated in a three-phase 12/8 SRM compared to a conventional controller. This controller is particularly suitable for transportation applications, especially for traction and propulsion in vehicles, due to its high average torque, low torque ripple, and fast dynamic response across various operating points.

articleTitle: Comparison between Phase-Shifted Full-Bridge and Full-Bridge LLC Topology for an Contactless Energy Transfer System for Ev's with Electrical Excitation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper deals with a comparison between a phase-shifted full-bridge topology and a full-bridge LLC topology for a contactless energy transfer system to supply the rotor of an electrically excited synchronous machine (EESM) for an electric vehicle (EV). The consideration is based on the special requirements of the application and on the use of the widebandgap semiconductor material gallium nitride (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{G a N}$</tex>). An operating point analysis of the electric machine in the WLTP cycle serves as the reference for the required transformer power. The comparison is carried out on the basis of component evaluations, simulations and measurements on a test arrangement.

articleTitle: A Reversible Substation for MVDC Railway Electrification System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: In order to improve the efficiency of railway lines electrified in 1.5 kV or 3 kV DC, the implementation of a Medium Voltage DC (MVDC) feeder-wire seems a relevant solution. This feed-wire, installed on the contact-line poles, allows the connection of renewable energy sources and storage systems. Thus, it is envisaged to use a reversible substation to interconnect the MVDC feed-wire and the AC public grid. When the traffic on the railway line is low, the reversible substation can provide both active and reactive power to support the three-phase utility grid. Consequently, this paper proposes a reversible MVDC substation based on three-level voltage source inverters. The different operating modes of the substation are first presented and illustrated by simulation results. The last part of the paper deals with the robustness of the reversible substation to withstand short-circuits on DC side.

articleTitle: A Novel Isolated Connector for Bidirectional Direct V2V Charging Using Onboard Chargers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel isolated connector designed for battery charging between two electric vehicles (EVs), To reduce costs and eliminate the need for a complex interfacing, it utilises the onboard chargers of both EVs while requiring two additional capacitors and a high frequency transformer (HFT). With the latter, the proposed connector provides gal-vanic isolation for safe vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) charging process. Because it involves a single-stage power conversion, the losses in the power devices are potentially low compared to other isolated topologies. In each charging cycle, not all devices of the existing chargers are utilised. Different set of switches can be selected for different charging cycle allowing each switch to experience an idling state, thus minimising its voltage and current stresses. The voltage regulation can be done in a similar way to a non-isolated pulse-width-modulation (PWM) controlled DC-DC converters making the conventional control schemes can still be applied. This paper describes in detail the operating principles of the connector, the derivation of its input-output voltage relationship and its application in charging the lithium-ion battery packs of either EVs. MATLAB/Simulink simulation results validate its functionality, demonstrating well-controlled transient performance. This connector has also been tested with the operation when constant-current control is required for charging a battery under different initial states-of-charge (SOCs).

articleTitle: Smooth Pole Change Method for Multiphase Induction Motor Drive System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: In this study, it is shown that the multiphase IM can be regarded as a superposition of independence, decoupled large-pole and small-pole IM by using the VSD conversion and multiphase IM drive system (IMTS: Induction Motor drive with Transmission System) that actively utilizes pole change is proposed. By deriving a mathematical formula, the factor of torque fluctuation response due to conflict of voltage limiter during pole number change is identified. In addition, the pole change law without torque fluctuation in multiphase IM is proposed by using the formula. An actual machine experiment is also conducted to confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Extended Analytic Selectivity Analysis of a Vehicular Electronic Fuse's Thermal Model-Based Wire Protection Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: To realize autonomous driving functions, a fail-operational vehicular power system is mandatory. This necessitates the selective isolation of short circuit faults and thermal wire overloads by the fusing elements. In future vehicular power systems, electronic fuses are inserted to implement an algorithm-based thermal wire protection. During the design process of the vehicular power system, the selectivity of the fusing elements has to be investigated and their selective coordination has to be ensured. The analytic triggering time determination represents an efficient methodology to examine the selectivity of wire protection algorithms of vehicular electronic fuses. In this contribution, an existing methodology is extended to consider also current measurement accuracy and hardware-related switching off delay in analytic selectivity analyses. Different types of current measurement accuracies are shown and corresponding analytic formulations are introduced. Using the extended methodology, the effect of the current profile parameters and the sampling time on the triggering time is examined. The sampling time can have a decisive influence on the triggering time and thus, the sampling time has to be considered in selectivity analyses. Furthermore, the selectivity of two cascaded eFuses with different current measurement accuracies is analyzed. For a given system which is selective in case of no measurement inaccuracy, it is shown that unfavorable constellations of the current measurement accuracies can lead to selectivity violations.

articleTitle: High Efficiency Smart Urban Mobility Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: There are many different public transportation methods. The energy efficiency of the different methods is one key comparison criteria. In this paper, a high efficiency smart urban method is highlighted, and its energy consumption is compared with the traditional mobility methods. The used data includes a real data from the public transport operator at Helsinki region, Finland and values from literature are used. The energy consumption of the urban track capsule is determined mathematically. The results show that there is a significant difference between the different transportation methods. This case study results come from relative cold climate and from an economic area of approximately one million inhabitants.

articleTitle: Model-Based Fault Diagnosis for Large-Scale Marine Battery Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Methods of fault diagnosis and prediction have become essential to the safe and economically viable operation of large-scale marine battery systems. However, these systems impose specific requirements limiting the usability of common approaches. In this study, a model-based fault diagnosis proce-dure is proposed, which utilizes a statistical system model in order to calculate the behavior deviations in a system requiring minimal computational effort and data availability. The proposed method is validated on both measured and artificially generated data of a 2 MWh system on a battery-hybrid vessel. The results show that the approach can successfully identify fault occurrences from the signal sequence.

articleTitle: Design Assessment of GaN FET-Based Inverter for Low-Voltage Braking System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper deals with a comprehensive design assessment of a Gallium Nitride (GaN)--based three-phase inverter for braking systems. The paper provides an overview of the GaN technology and a comparison with the Silicon MOSFET performances. Then, the GaN FET-based inverter is sized, taking into account the semiconductor losses (estimated from the datasheet and obtained from simulations). Furthermore, the cooling system is designed, and the steady state junction temperature of GaN FETs is obtained through thermal system simulations. Finally, the inverter input DC capacitor bank is sized, considering the chosen switching frequency and the root-mean-square current limits designed.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Investigation of Power Systems for a Decarbonized Naval Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper proposes a techno-economic investigation of power systems for a decarbonized naval sector. The goal is to build a database for the definition of cost functions related to the use of new green technologies in the naval sector and perform a comparison with conventional solutions. For this purpose, a state-of-the-art of the current technologies employed for power generation, storage and propulsion systems (in terms of power converters and electric motors) in the naval sector is presented. The work presents the set-up database, built on the base of commercially available data, that includes the main data of the technologies considered in terms of weights, volumes and costs. Finally, an analysis of the data collected is presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Rule-Based Strategy for Optimal Energy Management in Battery-Supercapacitor Hybrid Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The energy management strategy between the supercapacitor (SC) and the battery is a key focus of this paper, proposing an integrated approach that optimizes the utilization of both energy sources to enhance the overall performance and efficiency of electric vehicles. While existing energy management strategies for battery-SC hybrid systems have shown promise, they still face key limitations in the current literature. Many approaches focus either on rule-based methods or frequency separation techniques without effectively combining their strengths. Rule-based strategies often lack dynamic responsiveness to rapidly changing power demands, including regenerative braking scenarios, while frequency-based methods may not adequately consider the state of charge (SOC) for both the battery and the SC. Additionally, real-time implementation and computational efficiency remain challenges for more complex optimization-based approaches. This paper addresses these limitations by proposing an integrated strategy that combines rule-based and frequency decoupling methods to achieve responsive power distribution, effective SOC management, and efficient handling of regenerative braking energy. By effectively managing the interaction between the SC and battery, the proposed strategy demonstrates significant potential for improving the energy efficiency and sustainability of electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Driving Conditions Leading to Thermal Runaway in Li-Ion Battery Ev's
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The adoption of high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries (LIB) as the energy source in electric vehicles (EV) introduces significant safety concerns. Thermal runaway (TR), a self-accelerating rise in battery temperature resulting in catastrophic failure, is a significant safety concern. Cooling system failure within the EV's thermal management system is one of several factors that can trigger TR. Typically, TR is initiated by exceeding a critical temperature threshold under abusive conditions. Understanding the operating conditions that lead to the path of TR is essential for ensuring EV and occupant safety. Recently, a detailed electrochemical-thermal model that incorporates the chemical reactions within the battery until TR is introduced. This paper aims to illustrate how this model can be used to identify the conditions leading to TR under realistic EV driving scenarios. For this purpose, an Advisor/Matlabbased model of a hybrid EV is developed and verified by tests, is used to estimate the current required from the vehicle's battery pack at a given driving condition. This is followed by the prediction of battery thermal response using the mentioned finite-element-analysis-based battery model. Several scenarios are tested in this paper to determine whether TR occurs and to identify the factors contributing to TR. This study aids in comprehending the factors that contribute to TR and the development of preventative measures for battery management system design.

articleTitle: Comparative Energy Assessment of Automated Electric Vehicles Equipped With Acc Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper aims at conducting a comprehensive energy assessment of Automated Electric Vehicles equipped with two different type of ACC systems. By systematically comparing the energy performance of these two control strategies, insights about their respective efficiencies are provided under various driving conditions. The study involves rigorous testing and analysis, focusing on the energy consumption patterns of EVs operating under PI and MPC control schemes. The employed evaluation methodology integrates stochastic simulation with the PAWN sensitivity technique, in order to capture and quantify the impact of different driving variables on the energy output. The results of this research are expected to inform the development of more energy-efficient ACC systems, thereby enhancing the overall efficiency of EVs.

articleTitle: Continuous Wireless Power Supply with Solid-State Transformers for a Bidirectional Integrated System in a Light EV Using In-Wheel PMSM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper analyzes a continuous wireless power transmission system for light electric vehicles (EVs), intending to reduce battery weight and provide new opportunities for electromobility. A bi-directional integrated system using solid-state transformers is proposed to complement actual power electronics devices integrated into an experimental platform and used as a reference. Thus, a bi-directional electric energy flow is enabled anytime, even when the vehicle is running. Subsystems were individually verified through simulations followed by comprehensive system testing under a normalized driving cycle, through simulations. A high degree of control was verified for all intermediary voltage levels in the system components in parallel with the respect of torque and speed requirements. The results show opportunities for further deeper research and give perspectives for future developments.

articleTitle: Optimizing Fuel Consumption of a Dual-Fuel Full-Electric Vessel Using Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Full-electric vessels are a key component in the energy transition of the maritime sector. The design of optimal energy management (EM) is a significant challenge in making this technology more widely applicable. Taking into account developments for sustainable fuels and energy generation components often results in multi-component systems and dual-fuel vessels. The increased flexibility of those heterogeneous energy systems can result in suboptimal solutions for hybrid power-sharing using rule-based control. A solution to this problem is using predictive control strategies for optimal energy management. A promising approach is Model Predictive Control (MPC), which employs an internal model of the system to predict the system behavior over time and, therefore, optimize the operation in the longterm. This is especially helpful for managing the operation of several components simultaneously and can lead to increased energy efficiency and cost reductions overall. This paper presents a novel MPC controller for a dual-fuel DC full-electric vessel, incorporating diesel internal combustion engines, hydrogen fuel cells, and batteries with flexible changing operation conditions. The controller focuses on reducing operational costs by considering the economic weight of the fuels used and the future load demand forecast. The focus lies on the integration of mixed-integer aspects into the non-linear controller. An estimation of the saving potential is assessed in a simulation study comparing to a state-of-the-art rule-based controller and an instantaneous optimization controller. The results demonstrate the control's effectiveness in optimizing the operation. Further, we show the increase in fuel-saving potential by employing a future prediction.

articleTitle: Analytical Modeling and Parameter-Based Evaluation of Cooling Technologies for MW-Class High Specific Power Electric Motors in Electrified Aircraft Propulsion Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Power density and efficiency of electric motors in electrified drive trains are key aspects for electric aircraft propulsion. To increase both, temperature levels within electric machines must be decreased and high quantities of heat generated by electrical losses in critical components must be removed effectively. Hence, highly effective, capable and efficient cooling systems are crucial to enable electrification of aviation. A step towards an optimal cooling system for MW-class electric motors for electrified aircraft propulsion is to identify the most suitable cooling technique for each of the main heat sources within the machine. Goal of this paper is therefore to analytically model preselected cooling techniques, to define specific numerical parameters enabling their objective and reproductive evaluation and finally to perform their comparison aiming for identification of the optimal technologies in terms of high heat discharge ability and low energetic effort. Firstly, an analytical modeling of the thermal and fluid dynamical heat transfer processes for each of the preselected cooling techniques is executed. On this basis, comparative parameters are derived for each model to evaluate its effectiveness, capability and energetic efficiency of heat dissipation from the electric motor. Subsequently, identification of the optimal cooling technique for each component can be performed through comparison of the obtained comparative parameters. The results of the quantitative evaluation and comparison performed in this paper highlight the high potential of direct cooling technologies, especially in combination with forced convection and liquid coolants.

articleTitle: Energy Management Solution of the Future Dual-Mode Electric Train
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: As part of the agreements signed by the French government to guarantee the future of the country's secondary rail network, the regional transport authorities are looking for ways to reduce overall costs (purchase of equipment, operating and maintenance costs, etc.) while maintaining and even developing the transport offer on these lines. In this context, a new project called TELLi has been proposed. TELLi's ambition is to provide the regions with a solution that reduces the total costs of the railway system over its entire lifecycle. It proposes an innovative solution to replace the diesel rolling stock X73500 and X72500 currently used in this secondary rail network by autonomous electrical trains, which will be powered by catenary and modular energy sources: batteries and fuel cell. Consequently, this dualmode approach improves flexibility and efficiency in various railway operations, while simultaneously promoting energy efficiency and emission reduction. This paper develops a modelling and an innovative method for energy management to minimize the energy consumption of this novel train within the health conscious of the energy sources. Finally, simulation results of real train mission in French railway network will be presented to test and validate the energy management system.

articleTitle: Gradient-Based Predictive Pulse Pattern Control for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drives for traction applications are often operated at low switching frequencies to reduce losses. As, however, the switching frequency decreases, problems arise, such as high current distortions and poor dynamic performance. Optimized pulse patterns (OPPs) can be employed to improve the current quality, but they need to be properly handled to achieve good transient response. This papers presents a gradient-based direct model predictive control (MPC) algorithm for PMSM drives that manipulates OPPs in real time such that superior steady-state performance and fast settling times are achieved. The efficacy of the proposed method is tested with simulations, and its superiority over a field-oriented control (FOC) scheme is also demonstrated.

articleTitle: Small vs Large BEV and ICE Vehicles: A Few Real Life Clarifications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: Simple modelling often leads to valid general conclusions, but in some cases these simplifications do not apply equally to different systems, as is the case for energy consumption, in particular when comparing internal combustion engine (ICE) and electric vehicles (EVs). For instance basic vehicle modelling lead to broad brush statements like “small is efficient”. While this is substantially true for ICE powertrains, such commonsense statements turn out to be less accurate when real vehicles are concerned, in particular EVs. This paper attempts to qualitatively explain these discrepancies and underlines the importance of comparing real data with theoretical expectations, since “everything else being equal” does not always happen in reality and such results can at best be used as guidelines. The multiple impacts of battery size in this context are also analyzed, as well as considerations about real vehicle use and potential future regulatory approaches.

articleTitle: Design of a Test Bench for 1.5kV Solid State Circuit Breaker for Transport Electrification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper deals with the detailed design and laboratory testing methodology for a 1.5kV/70A Solid State Circuit Breaker (SSCB) for Medium Voltage Direct Current (MVDC) applications. The paper reviews the parameters and characteristics of wide bandgap semiconductors suitable for the protection of MVDC circuits. This consisting of detailed design process for the selection of the main MOSFET, transient voltage suppressors (TVS) to achieve the allowable voltage transient, current sensor, gate driver, and current limiting inductor for the selected di/dt limit. The laboratory testing methodology uses fast-acting IGBTs which allows for the application of short circuit faults in a controlled environment. The stiff DC grid is created by using an appropriately sized capacitor that holds energy of which only 1% is used for testing. The whole test bench has to be kept in an enclosure that is only opened once the capacitor voltage reaches a safe level. This is first of kind effort to achieve the short circuit fault clearing time of less than 2μs for an MVDC application.

articleTitle: Analysis of an Equivalent Consumption Minimization Strategy for a Fuel Cell Electric Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: This paper analyzes an energy management strategy known as Equivalent Consumption Minimization Strategy (ECMS) applied to the powertrain of a Fuel Cell Electric Aircraft. Such strategy is based on a pseudo-optimization algorithm whose goal is to minimize a cost index representing an equivalent fuel consumption for the powertrain. The equivalent fuel index is built by combining the real hydrogen consumed by the fuel cell and the electrical energy exchanged by the battery, which is converted into a virtual fuel consumption. The ECMS is assessed with the aid of a MATLAB/Simulink model of the powertrain, where a typical mission profile for the chosen aircraft is implemented. A comparison is drawn as well between the ECMS and a benchmark energy management strategy based on a rule-based state-machine algorithm. The analysis aims at providing deeper insight into the ECMS algorithm, and its results can be useful to design engineers for proper tuning and implementation of this strategy.

articleTitle: Lessons Learnt from High Impact R&D Projects from ZEWT and Other Sectors with ESS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Systems for Aircraft, Railway, Ship Propulsion and Road Vehicles & International Transportation Electrification Conference (ESARS-ITEC)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to cluster the main challenges and gaps for the safe integration of batteries in vessels, and for the improvement of the operation and performance of energy storage in the maritime sector. To do this, a benchmarking methodology was developed that compares technical and non-technical topics relevant to the identification and classification of EU-funded R&D projects with NEMOSHIP project. Firstly, the most relevant projects were selected considering the main topics of NEMOSHIP and their relationship with waterborne, electromobility, stationary or energy storage applications in general. Secondly, a weighting criterion is established for each project by evaluating the information available for each topic. In addition, the different technological trends, decisions, and roadmaps established in the most relevant and selected projects of the methodology are analysed. Finally, general conclusions and a compilation of lessons learned are presented from both a technical and non-technical perspective.

articleTitle: Power Density Optimization of 48V/12V DC-DC Converters Considering Several Topologies and Semiconductor Technologies
